recognize_zh: 兩顆嗜中性球核分葉不足：上方為兩葉以細絲相連的低分葉核，下方為不分節、形狀不規則的團塊核，且兩者細胞質淡而顆粒稀少，符合治療後成熟中的異常嗜中性球。
features: Two neutrophils of mature size with abnormal nuclear segmentation
Upper cell: bilobed (hypolobated) nucleus with two dense lobes joined by a thin strand, pseudo-Pelger-like
Lower cell: non-segmented, irregular, folded nuclear mass with coarse clumped chromatin
Pale, hypogranular grey-pink cytoplasm in both cells
Background normocytic red cells; no promyelocytes, Auer rods or blasts in field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells and two neutrophils with abnormal nuclear morphology. The upper neutrophil has a hypolobated bilobed nucleus with lobes joined by a thin chromatin strand, and the lower neutrophil has an irregular, non-segmented, folded nucleus; both show coarse mature chromatin and pale, hypogranular cytoplasm. No abnormal promyelocytes, Auer rods or blasts are present in this field. In the stated setting of ATRA/arsenic therapy for acute promyelocytic leukemia, findings are consistent with therapy-related maturation of leukemic cells into dysplastic-appearing neutrophils rather than a new myelodysplastic process.

ddx.vs: Morphology may be identical; the treatment history, transient nature (resolving within weeks) and absence of other dysplasia or MDS-defining genetics favor therapy effect.
The hereditary form affects virtually all neutrophils with normal granulation, unlike these hypogranular cells in a treated APL patient.
APL cells retain coarse azurophilic granules or Auer rods with less condensed chromatin, whereas these cells have mature clumped chromatin and sparse granules.
